note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 28, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The Royalist force remains local rather than assigning the mixed Royalist camp to Scotland alone; ENG PARL ARMY matches the Commonwealth of England.

Equipment review for Worcester: both complete forces use a representative British Civil War pike component. The Historic England report and Cromwell’s letter of 4 September 1651 document close pike fighting against the Royalist army. The National Army Museum armour supplies the period pot-helmet and armoured-pikeman analogy, without establishing a particular Scottish or English uniform or the prevalence of armour in 1651. The Royalist army remains a combined local force; neither army is represented as wholly composed of pikemen. No composition ratio, additional soldier count, casualty or death estimate is inferred. All CDB identities, sides and quantities remain unchanged.
